description: A three-tier HTTP service chain — gateway → service → datastore (checkout → inventory → datastore by default). Used by the reproduction engine as the system under test. Every service is a real process making real loopback HTTP calls under real timeouts, which is what makes a captured reproduction comparable to the incident it came from. Rename the services, or add a template of your own under reproduction/templates/, to model your own topology.
timeout_note: Each service's timeout is the value its own environment declares in environments/demo_commerce.json: inventory gives up on the datastore after 2500ms and checkout gives up on inventory after 2700ms. These are the magnitudes the demo incident's telemetry exhibits (datastore call 2500ms, inventory 2700ms, checkout 2900ms), so a reproduction can carry the same latencies instead of truncating the chain at an unrelated timeout.

expected_failure_semantics.datastore: latency above the caller's timeout makes inventory return 504; a dropped connection makes it return 503
expected_failure_semantics.inventory: a failing inventory call makes checkout return 503/504 and raises its own error rate
expected_failure_semantics.checkout: the furthest-downstream effect — it fails last and recovers last
